rows.stem:
Metal oxides generally react with acids, but few oxides of metal also react with bases. Such metallic oxides are :

I. \(\mathrm{MgO}\)

II. \(\mathrm{ZnO}\)

III. \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\)

IV. \(\mathrm{CaO}\)
rows.solution:
Oxides that react with both acids and bases to give salt and water are amphoteric oxides. Zinc oxide and aluminium oxide are amphoteric; magnesium oxide and calcium oxide are basic and react only with acids.

\(\mathrm{ZnO + 2NaOH \rightarrow Na_2ZnO_2 + H_2O}\) and \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3 + 2NaOH \rightarrow 2NaAlO_2 + H_2O}\)

This is option (B) II and III.

rows.stem:
Few drops of aqueous solution of ammonium chloride are put on a universal indicator paper. The paper turns pink.

Study the following table and choose the correct option.

options.label: A
options.text: Nature: acidic; Ammonium chloride is a salt of: weak acid and strong base; Range of pH: less than 7

options.label: B
options.text: Nature: basic; Ammonium chloride is a salt of: weak acid and strong base; Range of pH: more than 7

options.label: C
options.text: Nature: acidic; Ammonium chloride is a salt of: strong acid and weak base; Range of pH: less than 7

options.label: D
options.text: Nature: basic; Ammonium chloride is a salt of: strong acid and strong base; Range of pH: 7

rows.solution:
The pink colour on universal indicator paper shows that the solution is acidic, with a pH less than 7. Ammonium chloride is the salt of a strong acid (hydrochloric acid) and a weak base (ammonium hydroxide), which is why its solution is acidic.

This is option (C) Nature: acidic; Ammonium chloride is a salt of: strong acid and weak base; Range of pH: less than 7.

rows.stem:
Select the appropriate state symbols of the products given as X and Y in the following chemical equation by choosing the correct option from table given below :

\(\mathrm{Zn_{(s)} + H_2SO_{4(l)} \rightarrow ZnSO_{4(X)} + H_{2(Y)}}\)
rows.solution:
Zinc sulphate dissolves in water, so it is in aqueous solution, (aq). Hydrogen is given off as a gas, (g).

\(\mathrm{Zn(s) + H_2SO_4(aq) \rightarrow ZnSO_4(aq) + H_2(g)}\)

This is option (B) X: (aq); Y: (g).

rows.subtopic: Chemical Properties of Acids and Bases
rows.stem: Two salts ‘X’ and ‘Y’ are dissolved in water separately. When phenolphthalein is added to these two solutions, the solution ‘X’ turns pink and the solution ‘Y’ does not show any change in colour, therefore ‘X’ and ‘Y’ are
rows.solution:
Phenolphthalein turns pink only in a basic solution and stays colourless in an acidic or neutral one. Sodium carbonate is the salt of a weak acid and a strong base, so its solution is basic and turns pink. Ammonium chloride is the salt of a strong acid and a weak base, so its solution is acidic and shows no change.

(Sodium sulphate and sodium nitrate give neutral solutions, so neither can be the salt that turns pink.)

This is option (A) X: \(\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}\); Y: \(\mathrm{NH_4Cl}\).

rows.stem: In the given diagram of a closed stomata : (1), (2), (3) and (4) respectively are
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - a drawing of a closed stoma (two kidney-shaped cells side by side) with four parts marked by leader lines to the numbers (1), (2), (3) and (4); which structure each number points to is the quantity under test and is withheld here. Page idx 6.
rows.solution:
In the drawing, (1) points to the small dark oval body in the guard cell, the nucleus; (2) points to one of the many small dots, the chloroplasts; (3) points to the large clear central space, the vacuole; and (4) points to the kidney-shaped cell itself, the guard cell.

This is option (B) nucleus, chloroplast, vacuole, guard cell.

rows.subtopic: Human Brain and Protection of Nervous Tissue
rows.stem: Walking in a straight line and riding a bicycle are the activities which are possible due to a part of the brain. Choose the correct location and name of this part from the given table :

options.label: A
options.text: Part of the Brain: Fore brain; Name: Cerebrum

options.label: B
options.text: Part of the Brain: Mid brain; Name: Hypothalamus

options.label: C
options.text: Part of the Brain: Hind brain; Name: Cerebellum

options.label: D
options.text: Part of the Brain: Hind brain; Name: Medulla

rows.solution:
Walking in a straight line and riding a bicycle need posture, balance and precise voluntary movements. These are controlled by the cerebellum, which is a part of the hind brain.

This is option (C) Part of the Brain: Hind brain; Name: Cerebellum.

rows.stem: A student wants to obtain an erect image of an object using a concave mirror of 10 cm focal length. What will be the distance of the object from mirror ?
rows.solution:
A concave mirror forms an erect (virtual, enlarged) image only when the object is placed between the pole and the principal focus. With a focal length of 10 cm, the object must be less than 10 cm from the mirror.

This is option (A) Less than 10 cm.

rows.stem: Bronze is an alloy of
rows.solution:
Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin. (Brass is copper and zinc.)

This is option (D) Copper and Tin.

rows.stem: In an experiment with pea plants, a pure tall plant (TT) is crossed with a pure short plant (tt). The ratio of pure tall plant to pure short plants in \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation will be
rows.solution:
TT \(\times\) tt gives Tt in \(\mathrm{F_1}\). Selfing \(\mathrm{F_1}\) (Tt \(\times\) Tt) gives TT : Tt : tt = 1 : 2 : 1 in \(\mathrm{F_2}\).

Pure tall plants (TT) are 1 part and pure short plants (tt) are 1 part, so the ratio is 1 : 1, which is option (C) 1 : 1.

rows.stem: Study the given figure of a Food web and identify the primary consumer in the food web:
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - a food web of eight boxed organisms (Cat, Fox, Bear, Mice, Rabbit, Seeds, Plants, Grass) joined by arrows; which boxes the arrows link, and in which direction, decides the answer and is withheld here. Page idx 8.
rows.solution:
In the food web the arrows run from the food to the organism that eats it. Mice eat seeds and plants, and rabbits eat plants and grass, so mice and rabbits feed directly on the producers. They are the primary consumers. Cat, fox and bear eat mice or rabbits, so they are secondary consumers.

This is option (D) Mice and Rabbit.

rows.stem: Choose the correct order of the stages of binary fission in Leishmania.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - five drawings of Leishmania cells labelled (I) to (V) in a single box; which stage of division each drawing shows is the quantity under test and is withheld here. Page idx 10.
rows.solution:
In binary fission of Leishmania the nucleus divides first and the cell then splits lengthwise. So the order is: a cell with one nucleus (I); the nucleus divided into two, still close together (III); the two nuclei moved apart (II); the cell beginning to split lengthwise from one end (V); and the two daughter cells almost separated (IV).

This is option (B) I, III, II, V, IV.

rows.stem:
Consider the following chemical equation I and II

I. \(\mathrm{Mg + 2HCl \rightarrow MgCl_2 + H_2}\)

II. \(\mathrm{NaOH + HCl \rightarrow NaCl + H_2O}\)

The correct statement about these equations is –

options.label: A
options.text: ‘I’ is a displacement reaction and ‘II’ is a decomposition reaction.

options.label: B
options.text: ‘I’ is a displacement reaction and ‘II’ is double displacement reaction.

rows.solution:
In I, magnesium displaces hydrogen from hydrochloric acid, so it is a displacement reaction. In II, sodium hydroxide and hydrochloric acid exchange ions to give sodium chloride and water, so it is a double displacement (neutralisation) reaction.

This is option (B) 'I' is a displacement reaction and 'II' is double displacement reaction.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: In the following diagram showing dispersion of white light by a glass prism, the colours ‘P’ and ‘Q’ respectively are –
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - a ray marked 'White light' enters a triangular glass prism and two emergent rays leave it, labelled P and Q, with arcs marking their deviation from the dashed undeviated direction; which labelled ray is deviated more is the quantity under test and is withheld here. Page idx 10.
rows.solution:
Violet light bends the most and red light the least on passing through a prism. In the figure, P is deviated more from the original direction than Q, so P is violet and Q is red.

This is option (B) Violet and Red.

rows.stem: Consider the following three flowers namely X, Y and Z. Which flower(s) would develop into a fruit ?
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - a three-column table headed Flower X, Flower Y and Flower Z, each cell a drawing of a flower in longitudinal section; which reproductive parts each flower carries is the quantity under test and is withheld here. Page idx 12.
rows.solution:
Only a flower with a pistil (ovary) can develop into a fruit, since the ovary ripens into the fruit after fertilisation. Flower X has both stamens and a pistil, Flower Y has a pistil only, and Flower Z has stamens only.

So X and Y can develop into fruits, which is option (C) 'X' and 'Y' only.

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Solenoid
rows.stem: The magnetic field inside a long straight current carrying solenoid :

options.label: B
options.text: decreases as we move towards its end.

options.label: C
options.text: increases as we move towards its end.

rows.solution:
The field lines inside a long current-carrying solenoid are parallel straight lines, which shows that the magnetic field is the same at all points inside it (uniform).

This is option (D) is same at all points.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: In human eye the part which allows light to enter into the eye is –
rows.solution:
NCERT states that light enters the eye through a thin transparent membrane called the cornea, which forms the transparent bulge on the front of the eyeball. The marking scheme follows it. (The pupil, the opening in the iris that controls how much light passes on to the lens, can also be argued as the part that lets light in, so the choice Pupil is defensible.)

This is option (D) Cornea.

rows.subtopic: Chemical Properties of Acids and Bases
rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** It is advised that while diluting an acid one should add water to acid and not acid to water keeping the solution continuously stirred.

**Reason (R) :** The process of dissolving an acid into water is highly exothermic.
rows.context:
Q. No. 17 to 20 are Assertion – Reasoning based questions.

These consists of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
The Assertion is false: an acid must be added slowly to water with constant stirring, never water to acid. Adding water to a concentrated acid can make the mixture boil and splash the acid out, and the glass container may break.

The Reason is true: dissolving an acid in water is highly exothermic, which is exactly why the acid is added to the water.

The Assertion is false while the Reason is true, which is option (D).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** The energy which passes to the herbivores does not come back to autotrophs.

**Reason (R) :** The flow of energy in a food chain is unidirectional.
rows.context:
Q. No. 17 to 20 are Assertion – Reasoning based questions.

These consists of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Energy passed to the herbivores does not come back to the autotrophs, so the Assertion is true. This is because energy flows in only one direction in a food chain, from the producers to the consumers, so the Reason is true and explains the Assertion.

This is option (A).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Amoeba takes in food using finger like extensions of the cell surface.

**Reason (R) :** In all unicellular organisms, the food is taken in by the entire cell surface.
rows.context:
Q. No. 17 to 20 are Assertion – Reasoning based questions.

These consists of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Amoeba takes in food using temporary finger-like extensions of the cell surface (pseudopodia), which fuse over the food to form a food vacuole. The Assertion is true.

Not all unicellular organisms take in food through the entire cell surface: Paramecium, for example, takes in food at a specific spot, where cilia move it in. So the Reason is false.

The Assertion is true while the Reason is false, which is option (C).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Melting point and boiling point of ethanol are lower than that of sodium chloride.

**Reason (R) :** The forces of attraction between the molecules of ionic compounds are very strong.
rows.context:
Q. No. 17 to 20 are Assertion – Reasoning based questions.

These consists of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Ethanol is a covalent compound and melts and boils at low temperatures, while sodium chloride melts at about 1074 K. So the Assertion is true.

In ionic compounds such as sodium chloride, the positive and negative ions are held by strong forces of attraction, and a large amount of energy is needed to overcome them. So the Reason is true and explains the Assertion.

This is option (A).

rows.stem:
State whether the given chemical reaction is a redox reaction or not. Justify your answer.

\(\mathrm{MnO_2 + 4HCl \rightarrow MnCl_2 + 2H_2O + Cl_2}\)
rows.solution:
Yes, it is a redox reaction.

\(\mathrm{MnO_2 + 4HCl \rightarrow MnCl_2 + 2H_2O + Cl_2}\)

\(\mathrm{MnO_2}\) loses oxygen to become \(\mathrm{MnCl_2}\), so it is reduced. HCl loses hydrogen to become \(\mathrm{Cl_2}\), so it is oxidised. Since oxidation and reduction take place together, the reaction is a redox reaction.

rows.stem: List two differences between the movement of leaves of a sensitive plant and the movement of a shoot towards light.
rows.solution:
Any two:

| Movement of leaves of a sensitive plant | Movement of a shoot towards light |
|---|---|
| Not related to growth | Due to growth of the stem |
| Fast | Slow |
| Reversible | Irreversible |
| Not directional | Directional (towards the light) |
| Stimulus: touch | Stimulus: light |

rows.stem: What happens at synapse between two neurons ? State briefly.
rows.solution: At a synapse, the electrical impulse reaching the end of the axon of one neuron releases chemicals. These chemicals cross the small gap (the synapse) and start an electrical impulse in the dendrite of the next neuron. In this way the impulse is passed from one neuron to the next, in one direction only.

rows.stem: Give the name of the enzyme present in the fluid in our mouth cavity. State the gland which produces it. What would happen to the digestion process if this gland stops secreting this enzyme ?
rows.solution:
The enzyme in saliva is salivary amylase (ptyalin). It is produced by the salivary glands.

If the salivary glands stop secreting it, starch will not be broken down into sugar in the mouth. (Pancreatic juice in the small intestine also carries an amylase, so starch digestion would then be left to that stage.)

rows.stem: Let the resistance of an electrical device remain constant, while the potential difference across its two ends decreases to one fourth of its initial value. What change will occur in the current through it ? State the law which helps us in solving the above stated question.
rows.solution:
By Ohm's law, \(V = IR\), so with R constant the current is directly proportional to the potential difference. If V becomes \(\dfrac{V}{4}\), the current becomes \(\dfrac{I}{4}\): it decreases to one fourth of its initial value.

The law used is Ohm's law: the potential difference across the ends of a conductor is directly proportional to the current through it, provided its temperature remains the same.

rows.stem:
A light ray enters from medium A to medium B as shown in the figure.

(a) Which one of the two media is denser w.r.t. other medium ? Justify your answer.

(b) If the speed of light in medium A is \(v_a\) and in medium B is \(v_b\), what is the refractive index of B with respect to A.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - a horizontal boundary with a dashed normal, Medium 'A' below and Medium 'B' above, and a ray drawn from medium A into medium B; whether the ray bends towards or away from the normal decides part (a) and is withheld here. Page idx 16.
rows.solution:
(a) Medium B is denser. The ray bends towards the normal on entering medium B, so the angle of refraction is smaller than the angle of incidence (\(\angle r < \angle i\)). Light slows down on entering B, so B is optically denser than A.

(b) The refractive index of B with respect to A is

\(n_{BA} = \dfrac{\text{speed of light in A}}{\text{speed of light in B}} = \dfrac{v_a}{v_b}\).

rows.stem:
(a) A ray of light starting from diamond is incident on the interface separating diamond and water. Draw a labelled ray diagram to show the refraction of light in this case.

(b) Absolute refractive indices of diamond and water are 2.42 and 1.33 respectively. Find the value of refractive index of water w.r.t. diamond.
rows.solution:
(a) Diamond is optically denser than water, so a ray going from diamond into water bends away from the normal.

Diagram: draw the boundary with diamond on one side and water on the other, and a dotted normal at the point of incidence. Draw the incident ray in the diamond meeting the boundary obliquely, and the refracted ray in the water bending away from the normal. Mark the angle of incidence i and the angle of refraction r (with r greater than i), and draw arrows on the rays.

(b) The refractive index of water with respect to diamond is

\(n_{wd} = \dfrac{n_w}{n_d} = \dfrac{1{\cdot}33}{2{\cdot}42} \approx 0{\cdot}55\).

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Current-carrying Conductor
rows.stem: State the rule to determine the direction of a (a) magnetic field produced around a straight conductor carrying current and (b) force experienced by a current carrying straight conductor placed in a magnetic field which is perpendicular to it.
rows.solution:
(a) Right-hand thumb rule: hold the current-carrying straight conductor in the right hand with the thumb pointing in the direction of the current. The fingers then wrap around the conductor in the direction of the magnetic field lines.

(b) Fleming's left-hand rule: stretch the thumb, forefinger and middle finger of the left hand so that they are mutually perpendicular. If the forefinger points in the direction of the magnetic field and the middle finger in the direction of the current, the thumb points in the direction of the force (motion) on the conductor.

rows.stem: Explain the process of transport of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood in a human body.
rows.solution:
Oxygenated blood: oxygen-rich blood from the lungs comes to the left atrium of the heart through the pulmonary veins. The left atrium contracts and the blood passes into the left ventricle. The left ventricle then contracts and pumps the blood out to the body through the aorta.

Deoxygenated blood: deoxygenated blood from the body enters the right atrium through the vena cava. When the right atrium contracts, the blood passes into the right ventricle. The right ventricle then contracts and pumps it to the lungs through the pulmonary artery for oxygenation.

Valves between the atria and ventricles stop the blood flowing backwards, and the two kinds of blood are kept separate.

rows.stem:
A substance ‘X’ is used as a building material and is insoluble in water. When it reacts with dil. HCl, it produces a gas which turns lime water milky.

(i) Write the chemical name and formula of ‘X’.

(ii) Write chemical equations for the chemical reactions involved in the above statements.
rows.solution:
(i) X is calcium carbonate, \(\mathrm{CaCO_3}\) (limestone or marble).

(ii) With dilute hydrochloric acid it gives carbon dioxide:

\(\mathrm{CaCO_3 + 2HCl \rightarrow CaCl_2 + H_2O + CO_2}\)

Carbon dioxide turns lime water milky because insoluble calcium carbonate forms:

\(\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2 + CO_2 \rightarrow CaCO_3 + H_2O}\)

rows.stem:
A metal ‘M’ on reacting with dilute acid liberates a gas ‘G’. The same metal also liberates gas ‘G’ when reacts with a base.

(i) Write the name of gas ‘G’.

(ii) How will you test the presence of this gas ?

(iii) Write chemical equations for the reactions of the metal with (1) an acid and (2) a base.
rows.solution:
(i) The gas G is hydrogen, \(\mathrm{H_2}\).

(ii) Bring a burning candle (or splinter) near the gas: it burns with a pop sound.

(iii) The metal is zinc, which reacts with both acids and bases:

(1) \(\mathrm{Zn + 2HCl \rightarrow ZnCl_2 + H_2}\)

(2) \(\mathrm{Zn + 2NaOH \rightarrow Na_2ZnO_2 + H_2}\) (sodium zincate)

rows.stem: Name the gland and the hormone secreted by it in scary situations in human beings. List any two responses shown by our body when this hormone is secreted into the blood.
rows.solution:
In scary situations the adrenal gland secretes the hormone adrenaline.

Any two responses:

1. The heart beats faster, supplying more oxygen to the muscles.

2. The breathing rate increases.

3. Blood supply to the digestive system and the skin is reduced.

4. Blood is diverted to the skeletal muscles.

rows.stem:
In the given diagram

(i) Name the parts labelled A, B, and C.

(ii) Write the functions of A and C.

(iii) Reflex arcs have evolved in animals ? Why ?
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - a reflex-arc drawing: a hand over a hot pan, the arm, and a cross-section of the spinal cord, with three parts marked by leader lines to the letters A, B and C; which structure each letter marks is the quantity under test and is withheld here. Page idx 20.
rows.solution:
(i) A is the sensory neuron, B is the relay neuron in the spinal cord, and C is the effector, the muscle.

(ii) A carries the impulse from the receptor (in the skin of the hand) to the spinal cord. C responds to the stimulus by contracting, so the hand is pulled away.

(iii) Yes. Reflex arcs have evolved because the thinking process of the brain is not fast enough to protect the body in an emergency. A reflex arc responds quickly, without waiting for the brain to think.

rows.stem:
With the help of an appropriate example, justify that some of the chemical reactions are determined by

(a) Change in temperature,

(b) Evolution of a gas, and

(c) Change in colour

Give chemical equation for the reaction involved in each case.
rows.solution:
(a) Change in temperature: calcium oxide (quicklime) reacts vigorously with water and releases a large amount of heat.

\(\mathrm{CaO(s) + H_2O(l) \rightarrow Ca(OH)_2(aq)}\) + heat

(b) Evolution of a gas: zinc reacts with dilute sulphuric acid and bubbles of hydrogen are given off.

\(\mathrm{Zn(s) + H_2SO_4(aq) \rightarrow ZnSO_4(aq) + H_2(g)}\)

(c) Change in colour: blue copper sulphate crystals turn white on heating as they lose their water of crystallisation.

\(\mathrm{CuSO_4 \cdot 5H_2O \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} CuSO_4 + 5H_2O}\)

(An iron nail in blue copper sulphate solution, which turns the solution pale green, is an equally good example: \(\mathrm{Fe + CuSO_4 \rightarrow FeSO_4 + Cu}\).)

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.subtopic: Defects of Vision and their Correction
rows.stem:
State reasons for Myopia. With the help of ray diagrams, show the

(a) image formation by a myopic eye, and

(b) correction of myopia using an appropriate lens.
rows.solution:
Myopia (near-sightedness) is caused by (i) excessive curvature of the eye lens, or (ii) elongation of the eyeball.

(a) Image formation in a myopic eye: draw the eye with parallel rays coming from a distant object. After passing through the eye lens they meet at a point in front of the retina, not on it, so the distant object looks blurred.

(b) Correction: place a concave (diverging) lens of suitable power in front of the eye. The parallel rays from the distant object first diverge through the lens, as if coming from the far point of the myopic eye, and the eye lens then brings them to a focus on the retina.

Draw arrows on the rays to show their direction.

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Solenoid
rows.stem: What is a solenoid ? When does a solenoid behave as a magnet ? Draw the pattern of the magnetic field produced inside it showing the directions of the magnetic field lines.
rows.solution:
A solenoid is a coil of many circular turns of insulated copper wire wrapped closely in the shape of a cylinder.

It behaves as a magnet when an electric current is passed through it.

Diagram: draw a solenoid connected to a battery and a key. Inside it the magnetic field lines are parallel straight lines along its axis; outside they curve round from one end to the other, like those of a bar magnet, with one end acting as the north pole and the other as the south pole. Mark the direction of the current and the direction of the field lines.

rows.stem:
(a) Write the percentage of (i) solar energy captured by the autotrophs and (ii) energy transferred from autotrophs to the next level in a food chain.

(b) What are trophic levels ? Why do different food chains in an ecosystem not have more than four to five trophic levels ? Give reason.
rows.solution:
(a) (i) Green plants capture about 1% of the solar energy falling on their leaves.

(ii) About 10% of the energy is transferred from the autotrophs to the next level.

(b) Trophic levels are the various steps in a food chain at which the transfer of energy takes place.

Only about 10% of the energy at one level passes to the next. So the energy available keeps decreasing as we move to higher trophic levels, and very little usable energy remains after four or five levels. That is too little to support another level of organisms.

rows.stem:
(i) A compound ‘A’ with a molecular formula of \(\mathrm{C_2H_4O_2}\) reacts with a base to give salt and water. Identify ‘A’, state its nature and the name of the functional group it possesses. Write chemical equation for the reaction involved.

(ii) When the above stated compound ‘A’ reacts with another compound ‘B’ having molecular formula \(\mathrm{C_2H_6O}\) in the presence of an acid, a sweet smelling compound ‘C’ is formed.

(1) Identify ‘B’ and ‘C’.

(2) State the role of acid in this reaction.

(3) Write chemical equation for the reaction involved.
rows.solution:
(i) A, with molecular formula \(\mathrm{C_2H_4O_2}\), is ethanoic acid (acetic acid), \(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}\). It is acidic in nature. Its functional group is the carboxylic acid group, \(\mathrm{-COOH}\).

With a base such as sodium hydroxide it gives a salt and water:

\(\mathrm{CH_3COOH + NaOH \rightarrow CH_3COONa + H_2O}\)

(ii) (1) B, with molecular formula \(\mathrm{C_2H_6O}\), is ethanol (ethyl alcohol), \(\mathrm{C_2H_5OH}\). C is the sweet-smelling ester ethyl ethanoate (ethyl acetate), \(\mathrm{CH_3COOC_2H_5}\).

(2) The acid acts as a catalyst in this reaction (esterification).

(3) \(\mathrm{CH_3COOH + C_2H_5OH \xrightarrow{\text{acid}} CH_3COOC_2H_5 + H_2O}\)

rows.stem:
(i) Name the compound formed when ethanol is heated at 443 K in the presence of conc.\(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) and draw its electron dot structure. State the role of conc.\(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) in this reaction.

(ii) What is hydrogenation ? Explain it with the help of a chemical equation. State the role of this reaction in industry.
rows.solution:
(i) Heating ethanol at 443 K with excess concentrated sulphuric acid gives ethene, \(\mathrm{C_2H_4}\):

\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH \xrightarrow{\text{hot conc. } H_2SO_4} CH_2{=}CH_2 + H_2O}\)

Electron dot structure of ethene: the two carbon atoms share two pairs of electrons (a double bond), and each carbon shares one pair of electrons with each of its two hydrogen atoms. Every carbon then has eight electrons around it and every hydrogen two.

Concentrated sulphuric acid acts as a dehydrating agent: it removes water from ethanol.

(ii) Hydrogenation is the addition of hydrogen to unsaturated hydrocarbons in the presence of a catalyst such as nickel or palladium, giving saturated hydrocarbons. For example,

\(\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH_2 + H_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Ni catalyst}} CH_3{-}CH_3}\)

In general, a compound with a carbon-carbon double bond (\(\mathrm{R_2C{=}CR_2}\)) adds one hydrogen to each carbon to give \(\mathrm{R_2CH{-}CHR_2}\).

In industry it is used to convert vegetable oils (with unsaturated carbon chains) into vegetable ghee (fats with saturated carbon chains).

rows.stem:
Give reason for the following :

(a) During reproduction inheritance of different proteins will lead to altered body designs.

(b) Fertilization cannot take place in flowers if pollination does not occur.

(c) All multicellular organisms cannot give rise to new individuals through fragmentation or regeneration.

(d) Vegetative propagation is practised for growing only some type of plants.

(e) The parents and off-springs of organisms reproducing sexually have the same number of chromosomes.
rows.solution:
(a) DNA is the information source for making proteins. If the information is changed during DNA copying, different proteins will be made, and these will lead to altered body designs.

(b) In the absence of pollination, no pollen (male germ cells) reaches the stigma, so no male gametes are available to fuse with the female gamete in the ovule. So fertilisation cannot take place.

(c) In many multicellular organisms the specialised cells are organised into tissues, and tissues into organs, which occupy definite positions in the body. A piece of such an organism cannot regrow all of these, so simple fragmentation or regeneration is not possible.

(d) Vegetative propagation is used for some plants because (any one): plants grown this way bear flowers and fruits earlier than those grown from seeds; it allows plants such as banana, orange, rose and jasmine, which have lost the capacity to produce seeds, to be grown; the new plants are genetically similar to the parent and keep all its characteristics.

(e) During gamete formation the number of chromosomes is reduced to half. At fertilisation, the fusion of the male and female gametes restores the original number of chromosomes in the zygote, so the offspring has the same number as the parents.

rows.stem:
(i) What is meant by resistance of a conductor ? Define its SI unit.

(ii) List two factors on which the resistance of a rectangular conductor depends.

(iii) How will the resistance of a wire be affected if its

(1) length is doubled, and

(2) radius is also doubled ?

Give justification for your answer.
rows.solution:
(i) Resistance is the property of a conductor to resist (oppose) the flow of charges through it.

Its SI unit is the ohm (\(\Omega\)). The resistance of a conductor is \(1\,\Omega\) if a current of 1 A flows through it when the potential difference across its ends is 1 V, that is \(1\,\Omega = \dfrac{1\ \text{volt}}{1\ \text{ampere}}\).

(ii) Any two: the length of the conductor; its area of cross-section; the nature of its material; its temperature.

(iii) \(R = \rho\dfrac{l}{A} = \rho\dfrac{l}{\pi r^2}\).

When the length is doubled and the radius is also doubled,

\(R' = \rho\dfrac{2l}{\pi (2r)^2} = \rho\dfrac{l}{\pi r^2} \times \dfrac{2}{4} = \dfrac{R}{2}\).

The resistance becomes one half of its original value. (Taken one change at a time, doubling the length alone doubles the resistance to 2R, and doubling the radius alone makes it \(\dfrac{R}{4}\).)

rows.stem:
In an electric circuit three bulbs of 100 W each are connected in series to a source. In another circuit set of three bulbs of the same wattage are connected in parallel to the same source.

(i) Will the bulb in the two circuits glow with the same brightness ? Justify your answer.

(ii) Now, let one bulb in both the circuits get fused. Will the rest of the bulbs continue to glow in each circuit ? Give reason for your answer.
rows.solution:
(i) No, they will not glow with the same brightness.

In the series circuit the total resistance is three times that of one bulb, so the current is smaller, and the potential difference of the source is shared among the three bulbs. Each bulb gets only a third of the voltage, so it consumes much less power (\(P = \dfrac{V^2}{R}\) gives one ninth of its rated power) and glows dimly.

In the parallel circuit each bulb gets the full potential difference of the source, and so its full current, and glows with its normal brightness.

(ii) In the series circuit, if one bulb fuses the circuit is broken and the current stops, so none of the other bulbs glows.

In the parallel circuit the other two bulbs continue to glow with the same brightness, because each is connected directly across the source and still gets the same voltage.

rows.stem: Name the process of reduction used for a metal that gives vigorous reaction with air and water both.
rows.context:
On the basis of reactivity metals are grouped into three categories –

(i) Metals of low reactivity

(ii) Metals of medium reactivity

(iii) Metals of high reactivity

Therefore metals are extracted in pure form from their ores on the basis of their chemical properties.

Metals of high reactivity are extracted from their ores by electrolysis of the molten ore.

Metals of low reactivity are extracted from their sulphide ores, which are converted into their oxides. The oxides of these metals are reduced to metals by simple heating.
rows.solution: A metal that reacts vigorously with both air and water is highly reactive. It is obtained by electrolytic reduction: electrolysis of its molten ore (for example, of molten sodium chloride), in which the metal is deposited at the cathode.

rows.stem: Carbon cannot be used as a reducing agent to obtain aluminium from its oxide ? Why ?
rows.context:
On the basis of reactivity metals are grouped into three categories –

(i) Metals of low reactivity

(ii) Metals of medium reactivity

(iii) Metals of high reactivity

Therefore metals are extracted in pure form from their ores on the basis of their chemical properties.

Metals of high reactivity are extracted from their ores by electrolysis of the molten ore.

Metals of low reactivity are extracted from their sulphide ores, which are converted into their oxides. The oxides of these metals are reduced to metals by simple heating.
rows.solution: Aluminium is more reactive than carbon and has a greater affinity for oxygen, so carbon cannot remove the oxygen from aluminium oxide. Aluminium is therefore obtained by electrolytic reduction.

rows.stem: Describe briefly the method to obtain mercury from cinnabar. Write the chemical equation for the reactions involved in the process.
rows.context:
On the basis of reactivity metals are grouped into three categories –

(i) Metals of low reactivity

(ii) Metals of medium reactivity

(iii) Metals of high reactivity

Therefore metals are extracted in pure form from their ores on the basis of their chemical properties.

Metals of high reactivity are extracted from their ores by electrolysis of the molten ore.

Metals of low reactivity are extracted from their sulphide ores, which are converted into their oxides. The oxides of these metals are reduced to metals by simple heating.
rows.solution:
Cinnabar (HgS) is a sulphide ore of mercury, a metal of low reactivity. When it is heated in air, it is first converted into mercuric oxide. The mercuric oxide is then reduced to mercury on further heating.

\(\mathrm{2HgS + 3O_2 \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} 2HgO + 2SO_2}\)

\(\mathrm{2HgO \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} 2Hg + O_2}\)

Therefore metals are extracted in pure form from their ores on the basis of their chemical properties.

rows.solution:
| Roasting | Calcination |
|---|---|

rows.stem: In humans, how many chromosomes are present in a Zygote and in each gamete ?
rows.context: All human chromosomes are not paired. Most human chromosomes have a maternal and a paternal copy, and we have 22 such pairs. But one pair called the sex chromosomes, is odd in not always being a perfect pair. Women have a perfect pair of sex chromosomes. But men have a mismatched pair in which one is normal sized while the other is a short one.
rows.solution: A human zygote has 46 chromosomes (23 pairs), and each gamete has 23 chromosomes.

rows.stem: A few reptiles rely entirely on environmental cues for sex determination. Comment.
rows.context: All human chromosomes are not paired. Most human chromosomes have a maternal and a paternal copy, and we have 22 such pairs. But one pair called the sex chromosomes, is odd in not always being a perfect pair. Women have a perfect pair of sex chromosomes. But men have a mismatched pair in which one is normal sized while the other is a short one.
rows.solution: In some reptiles the sex is not decided by chromosomes. The temperature at which the fertilised eggs are kept decides whether the animals developing in them will be male or female.

rows.stem: “The sex of a child is a matter of chance and none of the parents are considered to be responsible for it.” Justify it through flow chart only.
rows.context: All human chromosomes are not paired. Most human chromosomes have a maternal and a paternal copy, and we have 22 such pairs. But one pair called the sex chromosomes, is odd in not always being a perfect pair. Women have a perfect pair of sex chromosomes. But men have a mismatched pair in which one is normal sized while the other is a short one.
rows.solution:
Father (XY) \(\rightarrow\) sperms: X or Y (in equal numbers)

Mother (XX) \(\rightarrow\) eggs: X only

Sperm X + egg X \(\rightarrow\) XX \(\rightarrow\) female child

Sperm Y + egg X \(\rightarrow\) XY \(\rightarrow\) male child

Each child has an equal (50%) chance of being a girl or a boy, depending only on which kind of sperm fuses with the egg. The mother always gives an X, so neither parent can be held responsible: the sex is a matter of chance.

rows.stem: Why do all the gametes formed in human females have an X chromosome ?
rows.context: All human chromosomes are not paired. Most human chromosomes have a maternal and a paternal copy, and we have 22 such pairs. But one pair called the sex chromosomes, is odd in not always being a perfect pair. Women have a perfect pair of sex chromosomes. But men have a mismatched pair in which one is normal sized while the other is a short one.
rows.solution: Human females have a perfect pair of sex chromosomes, XX (the 23rd pair). At gamete formation each egg receives one chromosome of every pair, so every egg gets one X chromosome.

rows.stem: List two properties of the image formed in Case I.
rows.context:
A student took three concave mirrors of different focal lengths and performed the experiment to see the image formation by placing an object at different distances with these mirrors as shown in the following table.

| Case No. | Object-distance | Focal length |
|---|---|---|
| I | 45 cm | 20 cm |
| II | 30 cm | 15 cm |
| III | 20 cm | 30 cm |
rows.solution: In Case I the object (45 cm) is beyond the centre of curvature (\(2f = 40\) cm), so the image is formed between F and C. Any two: it is real, inverted and diminished.

rows.stem: In which one of the cases given in the table, the mirror will form real image of same size and why ?
rows.context:
A student took three concave mirrors of different focal lengths and performed the experiment to see the image formation by placing an object at different distances with these mirrors as shown in the following table.

| Case No. | Object-distance | Focal length |
|---|---|---|
| I | 45 cm | 20 cm |
| II | 30 cm | 15 cm |
| III | 20 cm | 30 cm |
rows.solution: Case II. The focal length is 15 cm, so the centre of curvature is at 30 cm, and the object is placed at C. A concave mirror forms a real, inverted image of the same size at C itself.

rows.stem: Name the type of mirror used by dentists. Give reason why do they use such type of mirrors.
rows.context:
A student took three concave mirrors of different focal lengths and performed the experiment to see the image formation by placing an object at different distances with these mirrors as shown in the following table.

| Case No. | Object-distance | Focal length |
|---|---|---|
| I | 45 cm | 20 cm |
| II | 30 cm | 15 cm |
| III | 20 cm | 30 cm |
rows.solution: Dentists use concave mirrors. When the mirror is held close to the tooth (object between the pole and the focus), it forms an erect and enlarged image, so the tooth is seen in detail.

rows.stem: Look at the table and identify the situation (object distance and focal length) which resembles the situation in which concave mirrors are used as shaving mirrors ? Draw a ray diagram to show the image formation in this case.
rows.context:
A student took three concave mirrors of different focal lengths and performed the experiment to see the image formation by placing an object at different distances with these mirrors as shown in the following table.

| Case No. | Object-distance | Focal length |
|---|---|---|
| I | 45 cm | 20 cm |
| II | 30 cm | 15 cm |
| III | 20 cm | 30 cm |
rows.solution:
Case III. The object (20 cm) is closer to the mirror than the focus (30 cm), that is between P and F, which is how a shaving mirror is used. The mirror then forms a virtual, erect and enlarged image behind it. (By the mirror formula, \(u = -20\) cm and \(f = -30\) cm give \(v = +60\) cm and a magnification of 3.)

Ray diagram: draw a concave mirror with its pole P, focus F and centre of curvature C on the axis, and the object AB between P and F. From A draw a ray parallel to the axis, which after reflection passes through F; draw a second ray from A to the pole P, which reflects at an equal angle on the other side of the axis. The reflected rays diverge; produce them backwards with dotted lines to meet behind the mirror at A'. The image A'B' is behind the mirror, erect and larger than the object. Draw arrows on the rays.
